title: kbmon --events exports a refused query-log delivery as an ok span
goal: a kb.delivery span of a failed apply outcome (refused, failed) has status error, and carries no invented ms attribute

run:
import json,os,subprocess as s,sys,tempfile
H=tempfile.mkdtemp();q=os.path.join(H,'querylog');os.makedirs(q)
open(os.path.join(q,'distill.log'),'w').write('apply --push: refused: the push was refused\n')
E=dict(os.environ,CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA=H,CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=os.getcwd(),KB_COORD_STORE=os.path.join(H,'c.sqlite'))
d=json.loads(s.run([sys.executable,'_tools/kbmon.py','--events'],capture_output=True,text=True,env=E,timeout=120).stdout)
sp=[x for x in d.get('spans',[]) if x.get('name')=='kb.delivery']
if not sp: print('no kb.delivery span');sys.exit(1)
if sp[-1].get('status')!='error': print('failed delivery exported as %r'%sp[-1].get('status'));sys.exit(1)
print('ok: a refused delivery is a span in error')

notes: SP-qvlnptiw review (ST-gj4eicfw, ST-jx3c5vxm g1 changed): delivery_records builds the row with no exit, so status() returns ok next to the warn event.
